instructor: The instructor was efficient in the way he encouraged student participation, but he is prone to fixating on certain students as in favoring them over others, and doing the opposite for some students in the sense that he is overcritical of them and almost pedantic while grading their work. I have personally witnessed how he gave full points to students at a lower English level (with the condition that their skillset affected the overall integrity of the assignment) yet was overscrupulous when grading students at a level akin to that of a native speaker. I have also witnessed him being more lenient with students who are breaking the code of conduct (as in utilizing AI tools for graded assignments, which he took more strict precautions for later on) yet using an almost derogatory tone with others who ask questions about why he gave them the grades he did despite them always abiding by the rules. In conclusion, he seems to have a tendency to be biased while grading students’ work and I would not take another course from him or recommend others to do so.

instructor: He is very clearly unqualified to teach this course. He lacks adaptive and creative reading and thinking skills, thus unable to make necessary decisions. Furthermore, he does not understand the aspect of creativity in creative writing. He only defines "creative writing" within his limits of understanding of fiction, which is again, not so broad. Because of his lack of skills, he is also unable to create interactive, insightful discussions about texts or to deepen the conversations provided by the students.

Weakest Aspects (things he's bad at): Giving feedback, entering assignment points into relevant systems, being creative, having tolerance for different manifestations of creativity, understanding figurative language, reading & understanding the work he's supposed to give feedback for.
